title: Release comms handoff and customer notes template (mar-2026 draft)
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, ops-focused communications and handoff template for small-to-medium Redwood inference rollouts (hotfixes, minor model variants, feature toggles). The doc doubles as: 1) an internal ops checklist for release engineers and SREs and 2) a customer-facing release note + comms snippet that PMs / marketing can copy. Keep short; link to longer release notes when needed.

When to use this template:
- Mini-release or patch window (<= 48h stabilization expectation)
- Model variant swaps, routing policy flips, or control-plane config changes
- Customer-impacting behavior where we provide proactive notes (no full PRD change)

Quick release summary (TOP OF MESSAGE - single-paragraph for customers):
- Title: Rolling update: model routing tweak and latency improvements (non-breaking)
- ETA: 2026-03-18 09:00 PT -> 2026-03-18 11:00 PT (2h window)
- Impact: No downtime expected. A small percentage (~5%) of requests may be served by the old variant during the canary ramp. Users do not need to take action.

Internal ops handoff checklist (pre-release):
- [ ] Finalize PRs and attach release checklist: PR-1187 linked above
- [ ] Sign-off from Product: Priya Singh (email thread / slack)
content_continue:
- [ ] SRE smoke plan approved: SRE runbook id REL-SMOKE-7
- [ ] Release owner named and duty hours covered: Owner = Ava Chen, Backup = Diego Martinez
- [ ] Canary cohort definition documented: 5% traffic, region: us-west1, subset: tier=standard
- [ ] Telemetry gating thresholds set (see Telemetry section)
- [ ] Customer comms draft prepared and reviewed by PM/Marketing
- [ ] Post-release support rota assigned (72h watch)

Rollout calendar (hour-block plan for 2-hour window):
- T-minus 60m: final CI build validation, export artifact, tag release: v2026.03.1187
- T-minus 30m: announce start in #release-orchestra and pagerduty (ops-team)
- T-minus 15m: switch to maintenance branch for infra changes (if needed)
- T0: enable canary routing (5% traffic -> variant B)
- T+15m: smoke tests (fast paths) and latency check
- T+30m: telemetry gating decision point 1 (see gating rules)
- T+45m: increase cohort to 25% if stable
- T+90m: full ramp to 100% or deploy fallback per policy
- T+120m: post-rollout snapshot + initial retro notes (owner)

Telemetry gating rules (explicit numbers for quick decision):
- Latency: p95 <= 400ms (steady-state for the route). If p95 increases > 30% over baseline for 10m, fail and rollback.
- Error rate: 5xx rate <= 0.1% of requests in the canary cohort. If > 0.5% for 5m, fail and rollback.
- Quality signal: model-level degradation measured via prompt-set A (automated eval). If semantic-similarity drop > 4% vs baseline, pause ramp and notify ML lead.

Smoke test checklist (commands and quick checks):
- [ ] Health endpoints: curl -sS https://api.redwood.ai/health | jq .status == "ok"
- [ ] Sample generation: run local script smoke/generate_smoke.sh --model variantB --seed 42 and compare token counts
- [ ] KV cache warmup: verify cache hit-rate > 60% after 10 warmup requests
- [ ] Metrics snapshot: export p95/p99 and error counters to /tmp/snapshots/release-$(date +%s).json

Rollback criteria and immediate steps:
- Criteria: any gating rule failure, sustained CPU/GPU saturation >95% for 10m, or customer escalations that match severity 1/2 patterns
- Immediate steps (owner + on-call):
  1) Notify #release-orchestra and page on-call (pagerduty)
  2) Flip routing back to previous stable variant (route -> variantA) using routing CLI: redwood route set --route chat-gen --variant variantA --force
  3) Mark release as "rolled-back" in release tracker and open incident placeholder (REL-INC-####)
  4) Collect traces, core metrics, and a 30m pre/post diff and attach to the incident

Customer-facing release notes (full template to copy into support portal / newsletter):
- Short headline (1 line): Improved latency and model routing stability for chat generation
- TL;DR (2-3 lines): We rolled out a targeted routing update to reduce tail latency on chat-generation routes. No action required on your side. You may occasionally see responses generated from the previous variant while the rollout finishes.
- What changed (bullet list):
  - Adjusted serving routing to prefer quantized variant in low-latency path
  - Tuned caching for short prefix reuse (saves ~6% token cost in internal tests)
  - Minor safety rule tweak: reduced false positive blocking on benign assistant prompts
- Impact and roll-out schedule: Starting 2026-03-18 09:00 PT, gradual roll to all regions over 2 hours.
- Troubleshooting / contact: If you notice degraded latencies or unexpected outputs, please email support@redwood.ai with subject "Release 2026-03-18 feedback" or open a support ticket.

Post-release actions (first 72 hours):
- [ ] 0-2h: Owner posts initial snapshot, update Slack thread with p95/p99 and errors
- [ ] 2-8h: Run automated prompt-set B to detect quality drift (owner + ML lead)
- [ ] 8-24h: Customer inbox triage; route tickets to on-shift SE
- [ ] 24-72h: Retro and lesson log: capture what went well, what blocked, one improvement to process

Playbook notes / tips (ops tribal knowledge):
- Keep the customer note short and optimistic; avoid technical jargon beyond one-liners (customers skim).
- If a rollback is performed, include the exact command and timestamp in the incident note so downstream teams can correlate logs and traces.
- For canaries where we expect small differences in outputs (model variant differences), include a short sample in the private incident to help engineering reproduce.
- Use the telemetry snapshots to build a short graph for the retro — ops people read graphs faster than paragraphs.

Appendix: quick templates (copy/paste)
- Slack start announcement (ops):
  Heading: "Release window start: routing tweak (owner: Ava Chen)"
  Body: "Starting canary now (5% -> variantB) in us-west1. TL;DR: watch p95 and 5xx. Runbook: <link>. Pagerduty: on-call-eng. Will post updates at T+15m, T+30m."

- Customer one-line (support reply):
  "Thanks for reporting — we deployed a routing update on 2026-03-18. We're looking into the behavior you saw; can you paste a request id if available?"

- Retro prompt (owner to fill after stabilization):
  1) What surprised us?
  2) What did our gates catch? What did they miss?
  3) One small change to the checklist for next time

Contact / escalation matrix:
- Release owner: Ava Chen (ava@redwood.ai)
- Backup owner: Diego Martinez (diego@redwood.ai)
- ML lead: Priya Singh (pri@redwood.ai)
- SRE primary: Lars Becker (lars@redwood.ai)
- Support escalation: Emma Johnson (emma@redwood.ai)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Confirm whether the short-prefix cache size needs a config flag for private deployments (action: Priya)
- Validate canary cohort selection in eu-west1 to match us-west1 (action: Diego)
- Draft customer blog short-note if rollout reaches >50% traffic without issues (action: Product)
